title: Season standings not computed — get_competition_standings is a stub
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:887-893 returns {"message": "...would be calculated here"}; no points/positions aggregated from matches. CONFIRMED on re-check — the function body is a placeholder, not an implementation.
suggestion: Aggregate match results into a points table (3/1/0), compute GF/GA/GD, sort to produce positions.

title: BR-Football-Dataset columns mis-mapped — ~9,173 matches loaded with garbage fields
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:282-287 reads row[2]=away_team, row[3]=home_goals, row[4]=away_goals, row[7]=date; actual header is tournament,home,home_goal,away_goal,away,...,date(idx12). Loader output: {home_team:'Sao Paulo', away_team:'1.0', home_goals:'1.0', away_goals:'Flamengo', date:'75.0'}. Serie A/B/C totals = 3689+3677+1807 = 9173 garbage rows. CONFIRMED.

title: novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (6,886 matches) loads zero rows — wrong delimiter
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:93-105 splits on ';' but the file is comma-separated (header has 13 comma-fields, 1 semicolon-field). len(parts)<10 skips every row. Loaded Brasileirão count == 4180 == Brasileirao_Matches.csv alone (4181 lines − header); novo contributed 0. CONFIRMED.
suggestion: Split on ',' (or use csv.reader); the file uses ID,Data,Ano,Rodada,Equipe_mandante,Equipe_visitante,Gols_mandante,Gols_visitante,... columns.

title: Tests under-verify — return bools, import nonexistent mcp.server.MCPServer, coverage 0.49
evidence: test_brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:26 imports MCPServer (does not exist; except swallows it); tests return booleans rather than asserting; integration_test.py functions return bool (PytestReturnNotNoneWarning). 5 tests 'pass' but assert nothing about correctness.
suggestion: Use assert statements that check concrete query results against expected values from the datasets.

title: .isdigit() silently zeroes decimal '3.0'-style scores in aggregates
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:603-604, 791-792, 836-837 use match['home_goals'].isdigit() — False for '1.0'/'3.0', so BR-Football-style decimal scores become 0 in statistics.
suggestion: Parse goals with float()/int(float()) under try/except rather than .isdigit().

title: get_head_to_head uses unguarded int() on goal strings
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:942-943 call int(match['home_goals']) with no guard; a non-integer goal string (e.g. corrupted BR-Football row) would raise ValueError and crash the tool.
suggestion: Guard with try/except or reuse a shared safe-int helper.
